discovery: Photonic crystals and the photonic band gap: controlling the propagation, localization and emission of light in periodic dielectric media
subfield: Optics and photonics / wave physics in structured media
motivation: In 1987, Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that a periodic dielectric structure can open a complete photonic band gap, a frequency range in which light cannot propagate at all. Yablonovitch showed that such a gap suppresses spontaneous emission, rewriting a basic rule of light-matter interaction, and then built the first three-dimensional photonic crystal ('Yablonovite'). John showed that near the gap, disorder can produce strong Anderson localization of light, bringing a central idea of condensed-matter physics into optics. Together these ideas founded photonic crystals, now a major field. It underlies photonic-crystal fibres, high-Q nanocavities for cavity QED and quantum photonics, slow light, integrated silicon photonics and, later, topological photonics. Their work changed how physicists think about waves in all structured media, from electrons and phonons to cold atoms, and it has had a lasting impact on technology. I nominate them jointly.
